title: 'Dreamy Blues', 'C Jam Blues' and which tunes were his
summary: He denies writing 'C Jam Blues' and lets Europeans think so; 'Saturday Night Function' and 'Stompy Jones' are right, and he recorded it first with his small group.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Also on these liner notes, Barney, it says, "Probably the best known of Bigard's own contributions to the monumental Ellington book of originals is the sultry Mood Indigo, originally titled "Dreamy Blues.""
Is that right? We didn't -- "Dreamy Blues?"
Not as I know of.
I never read that title before.
No.
The now classic clarinet-trombone There were other Bigard contributions, such as "Rocking in Rhythm," "Stompy Jones," "Saturday Night Function," and "C Jam Blues."
Well, --
What about --
-- some of it is wrong.
What is wrong?
"C Jam" is wrong to begin with.
Stompy Jones is okay. What's that other one you --
"Saturday Night Function" and Rocking in Rhythm which we --
Yeah, "Saturday Night Function" is right.
But I think Rex Stewart also mentions -- credits "C Jam" Blues to you but he says you said that you wrote it, that you --
No, I didn't tell Rex. He's day-dreaming.
Who wrote "C Jam" Blues? Do you know?
"C Jam" Blues? Duke, I think. I don't know.

In his chapter, "Illustrious Barney Bigard," in Rex's book Jazz Masters of the Thirties, Rex says, "In addition to joining in the jollity, Barney also was inspired to create melodies during those Ellington days. Among the credits he claims are "Mood Indigo," "Saratoga Swing," "Minuet in Blue," "Saturday Night Function," "Stompy Jones," "Clouds in My Heart," "Rocking in Rhythm." There are many others, too, that he sold or gave away."
So I guess he doesn't say "C Jam". I beg your pardon.
But I have read someplace else in some of the material --
Uh-huh.
-- that somebody else said that you wrote "C-Jam."
Yeah, but they were wrong. They even believed it, all in Europe, that I wrote that. So I just let them think it.
It was first called C Blues, right? And you recorded it with your small unit, didn't you?
Yes, I recorded it first and then they got the big band together, I guess, and -- [LONG PAUSE]
